newsitem.title: UK: British call on Japanese to end scientific whaling.
newsitem.headline: British call on Japanese to end scientific whaling.

text.p: The British government on Friday called upon Japan to discontinue its scientific whaling operations in the Antarctic.

The move comes just days after the environmental group, the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF), claimed that a Japanese factory ship was setting off to hunt 440 minke whales in the Southern Ocean Whale Sanctuary.

"We are very disappointed that Japan has decided to ignore the resolution adopted at this year's meeting of the International Whaling Commission calling on it to abandon its plans to carry out scientific whaling in the Southern Ocean Sanctuary," Fisheries Minister Tony Baldry said in a statement.
"We are asking Japan to think again and to respond positively to the request from the great majority of IWC members to abandon research that involves killing whales."
Japan has ignored a resolution adopted at the International Whaling Commission(IWC) in Scotland earlier this year calling on it to abandon its whaling operations.
Although Japan's scientific whaling is not illegal under international legislation, a number of IWC member nations call for it to be ended each year.
The WWF claims that scientific whaling involves whale meat being cut and processed on board a factory ship and sold to the Japanese market.
